Stylised hiragana あ ("a") . The emblem also expresses sunrise and wave to indicate Aichi's location facing the Pacific Ocean.
Stylized katakana character ア ("a") on a dark red field.
Stylised map of the prefecture in green on a white field.
A blue field with チバ ("Chiba") stylized into a rapeseed flower.
Horizontal tricolor of yellow, green and yellow with an orange blossom.
A dark blue field charged with a circular emblem consisting of the katakana フクイ ("Fukui") stylized into a young leaf growing next to two other leaves.
The hiragana ふく ("fuku") stylized into a plum blossom.

An orange field with the hiragana character ふ ("fu") stylized into a circle toward the hoist side. The slightly off-center placement is said to represent "strength and endless progress".[3] It is also reminiscent of the shape of a peach, as Fukushima is one of the top peach producing regions in Japan.[4]
A white field charged with a green stylized "岐" ("gi") inside of a green circle.
A purple field charged with three crescents and the old version of “群” (“gun”) with “君” on the top and “羊” on the bottom.
Katakana character ヒ ("hi") stylized into two attached circular crescents on a maroon red field.
A navy blue field charged with a red 7-pointed star with a thick white fringe around the star.
Kanji character 兵 ("Hyō") stylized into waves on a light blue field.
A white stylized rose bud on a field of indigo.
Stylized kanji of 石川 (Ishikawa) on a cerulean blue field.
A bluish-gray field charged with the kanji 岩 (iwa) stylized with vertical and horizontal symmetry.
An olive green field charged with a stylized and rotated katakana カ ("ka").

A black horseshoe shape (representing the Satsuma and Osumi Peninsulas) with a small dent on the bottom-right corner of the emblem (representing Shibushi Bay) surrounding a red circle (representing Sakurajima).
Stylized Kanji character 神 (the first character from 神奈川 "Kanagawa") in red on a white field.
A maroon red field charged with と ("to", from Tosa) and コ ("ko", from Kōchi) stylized into a sword pointing up.
A maroon field charged with a white ク ("ku") reminiscent of the shape of Kyushu.
A violet field charged with a white 6-petal flower with a yellow dot in its center.
A green field charged with a white み stylized into an arrow pointing up.
A green field charged with a white み stylized into a Lespedeza thunbergii (known locally as miyaginohagi (ミヤギノハギ)).
A green field with a yellow ミ ("mi") stylized into three stairs.
An orange field charged with a white disc consisting of a stylized katakana "ナ" (na).
A white field charged with a light blue N stylized into the form of a dove.
A white field charged with a maroon ナ ("na") stylized as a circle.
Red field charged with a gold stylized 新 ("nii") and Katakana characters ガタ ("gata").
A white field charged with three red kanji 大 ("ō") stylized and arranged in a circle. The variant has the prefecture's full name in kanji at the bottom-hoist (left) corner.
A dark purple field charged with a yellow 岡 ("oka") stylized as a circle.
A white field charged with a white O inside of a red disc.
A blue field charged with three white letter "o"s connected via branches to another "o".
A green field charged with a white camphor flower.
A white field charged with 16 red ornamental beads arranged in a circle. The 玉 ("tama") of "Saitama" means "bead".
A light blue field charged with a white emblem consisting of シガ ("Shiga") stylized into a circle with wings.
A dark red field charged with four yellow katakana マ (ma) circularly stylized and arranged into a cloud-shaped circle
A blue field with an orange emblem consisting of a stylization of both the map of the prefecture and Mount Fuji. the emblem is thickly fimbriated with white.

A light green field charged with an emblem consisting of the kanji 栃 ("tochi"), heavily stylized. The top-left corner of the emblem is a white rectangle with three upward-pointing arrows, a stylization of the character 木 ("gi").
A blue field charged with a yellow emblem consisting of the hiragana とく ("toku") stylized into a flying bird. The variant has the prefecture's full name in kanji at the bottom-fly (right) corner.

A six-rayed stylised sun with a dot in the center. The background color is Edo purple (江戸紫, Edo murasaki), which was popular in Edo, the name of Tokyo during the Edo period. This shade of purple is one of the traditional colors of Japan, and is near-identical to Web Indigo.

A stylised green Ginkgo biloba leaf. The symbol consists of three arcs combined to resemble a leaf of the ginkgo, the metropolitan tree, and is reminiscent of a "T" for Tokyo. Created by Rei Yoshimura (レイ吉村), a professional graphic designer.
A blue field charged with a white emblem consisting of the hiragana と ("to") stylized into a flying bird ("tori").
A white field charged with a green emblem consisting of the hiragana と ("to") stylized together with Mount Tateyama.
A white field charged with a navy blue emblem, consisting of the katakana ワ ("wa") stylized into an open fan.
A blue field charged with three white mountain peaks (possibly stylizations of the kanji for mountain 山, "yama") with a triangular indentation on the bottom of each peak.
A brown field charged with the kanji 山口 ("Yamaguchi") stylized into a bird flying towards the sun.
A magenta field charged with three orange stylized 人 combined to form a 山 ("yama") enclosed by a white trapezoid representing Mount Fuji.
